text: The gap arises because a human’s basic aspiration for happiness and prosperity cannot be satisfied by physical facilities alone. Without nurturing relationships and cultivating a correct self‑understanding, one remains in an animal‑level, purely material consciousness. The lack of these three dimensions—physical, relational, and introspective—creates the disconnect between what one wants and where one currently is.

To fill the gap between animal and human consciousness, we must ensure physical facility is maintained while prioritizing relational fulfillment and cultivating right understanding through education and holistic development.

text: I see my role in the education system as facilitating holistic development by ensuring education extends beyond material provision to foster healthy relationships and self-understanding, guiding learners from an animal to a human consciousness.

The fundamental difference is that while animals achieve well‑being with sufficient physical facilities alone, human beings require additional elements—meaningful relationships with other humans and right self‑understanding—to attain true happiness; thus, education must address these dimensions to transform animal consciousness into human consciousness.

Holistic development is the transformation of a person from animal consciousness to human consciousness. It requires the integration of physical facility, healthy relationships with other humans, and a correct understanding of oneself. Education–sanskar is the vehicle that facilitates this transformation by cultivating these three components.

Living with animal consciousness means relying solely on physical facilities for fulfillment. In contrast, living with human consciousness requires three elements: physical facility, meaningful relationships with other people, and a correct understanding of the self. The correct priority is to secure physical facilities first, then nurture relationships, and finally develop the right understanding, thereby achieving human consciousness.
